The only nontrivial local stabilizers are C2, and connectedness of the singular knot makes their nontrivial generators conjugate to the meridian. The A8 quotient factors through meridian squares. In the transposition-edge graph of r double transpositions, components are exactly group orbits; transitivity on eight letters requires at least seven edges and hence r >= 4. checkedDeductions.assessment: Corollary 6 requires no parity: images of bridge-meridian involutions generate the target by torsion or identities. Corollary 7 uses the explicitly parity-preserving preorder only where the imported BKN theorem requires it. For knot sources the C2 abelianization forces parity compatibility of every epimorphism. The closed hyperbolic cover is a prime factor without a Seifert JSJ piece, also in the stated trefoil-sum targets. The determinant hypothesis is retained for links; the U4 free-product map is parity preserving and realizes b(U4) = 4 under the stated broad arborescent convention.

With the specified column-vector Fox convention, M injects the b top-cap colours and L imposes the bottom-cap equalities. A common prime divisor of every entry makes LRM zero over Fp, leaving a b-dimensional colouring space. Using the expressly imported reduced-colouring/H1 dimension identity gives dim H1 = b - 1 >= 3 since every such plat has b >= 4. This contradicts the integral cyclicity bound. The argument quantifies over every plat satisfying the nonunit condition and handles the all-zero matrix case. It does not classify unit-gcd generalized Montesinos descriptions or the separate general matrix/Fox-ideal criterion.

The low Alexander coefficients follow from the displayed formula, the homogeneous braid data agree with the displayed word, and the stated Rasmussen/genus comparisons are consistent. The elementary cable breadth argument is valid once bridge number forces winding two; Whitehead patterns have genus at most one. The Coxeter and augmentation exclusions are consequences of the stated family bounds only for constructions supplying the specified sharp certificates. The text preserves the universal fishnet/plain-sphere statements, arbitrary meridionally tame bases, arbitrary quasipositivity, and priority limits.

checkedRSRelators: For the index-two parity subgroup with transversal {1,a}, s(1,mu_i) = mu_i a^-1 = u_i and s(a,mu_i) = a mu_i = v_i; u_0 is trivial and v_0 = a^2.
Rewriting each square relator mu_i^2 from the two cosets gives u_i v_i and v_i u_i. The base square kills v_0. Eliminating v_i = u_i^-1 is correct and imposes no u_i^2 = 1 relation.
After all meridians are involutions, either crossing sign admits the relator mu_out mu_over mu_in mu_over. Its first rewrite is R = x_out x_over^-1 x_in x_over^-1.

The other-coset rewrite is x_out^-1 x_over x_in^-1 x_over. This equals x_out^-1 R^-1 x_out, so it is redundant. Together with the square relators these account for the Reidemeister-Schreier relators of the given orbifold presentation.
dimensionArgument: Identifying the parity kernel with the fundamental group of the branched double cover, the abelianized presentation has x_0 = 0 and x_out + x_in - 2x_over = 0 at each crossing.
Homomorphisms from this abelianization to Fp are exactly Fox colourings with base colour zero. Every colouring splits uniquely into its constant base colour plus a based colouring.
The Hom space is the dual of H1 of the branched cover with Fp coefficients and therefore has the same dimension. No division by 2 occurs, so the argument includes p = 2.
In the plat application, LRM = 0 mod p leaves b independent top-cap colours. Lemma 9 then forces dim H1 = b - 1 >= 3, contradicting cyclicity. The changed application is internally correct.
